item.description:
UNO Wild Jackpot is a spin on traditional UNO that incorporates a slot machine-style device and re-writable custom rules cards.
Before the game begins, players come up with their own unique custom rules and write them on the dry erase custom rules cards. These are shuffled and inserted into the back of the slot machine.
During the game, which plays exactly like standard UNO, you can play a special Jackpot card to pull the lever on the slot machine. This spins a random result on the center wheel, such as dispensing one of the custom rules to a player at the table who must then follow that rule.

item.description:
Players draw hands of tiles with color and number and arrow markings.
Much like in the card-based UNO, each player must play the next tile that matches either the color or number of the previous one played. However in UNO Wild Tiles, they must play it on the space indicated by the arrow on the previous tile, and may place their own tile so that the arrow suits them.
Winner is the first to clear their rack, or the person with the fewest points when it is impossible to play any more tiles.

item.description:
UNO Zero is a table top card game, where the goal is to score as low as possible (ideally zero points hence the name). Each player at the beginning has a set of six cards faced down in front of them. The grid consists of three columns and two rows. At the beginning each player can turn and reveal two of their cards. After that all players attempt to reveal all their face-down cards by drawing one card each turn from the discard or draw pile and exchanging them with one of their cards. Two cards of the same colour or the same number in one column are discarded. That way players can get rid of their points.
What's special about UNO zero is that the typical UNO action cards are part of this game. The reverse card changes the direction of the game. The draw two or draw 4 card makes players add more columns to their grid. And the skip card has the next player skip their turn.
That makes this game vey dynamic, surprising and fun. Each round is different and you can get very lucky and have only two cards left at the very end, or unlucky and you still have 12 cards in front of you while another player finishes the game.
Once there is only one face-down card left in your grid you have to say UNO or you'll be punished to draw two more cards. It's easy to learn and start, since the rules are quickly explained and the famous UNO action cards almost anybody already knows. —description from the publisher

item.description:
UNO: Reverse Pack Add-On of 16 cards adds chaotic fun to the classic UNO game by introducing a variety of enhanced reverse cards. This pack includes new twists like Reverse Draw 2, Reverse Skip, Wild Power Reverse, and the unique Wild NO U card. Reverse Draw 2 reverses the direction and forces the next player to draw two cards, skipping their turn. Reverse Skip reverses the direction and skips the next player's turn entirely. The Wild Power Reverse lets you reverse play direction, pick the next color, and take another turn. The Wild NO U card can counter any draw-card action, reversing its penalty back to the previous player and changing the color, or simply act as a standard wild card with reverse functionality. These cards add strategic depth and unpredictability, requiring players to stay alert and adjust quickly.
—description from the rulebook (adapted)

item.description:
UNO: Speed Pack Add-On of 16 cards introduces a new level of excitement to the classic UNO card game by speeding up gameplay and challenging players to match the increasing speed. Each "Speed Up" icon played raises the number of cards all players must play on their subsequent turns, starting from the next player. Initially, each player plays one card per turn, but with each "Speed Up" card played, this number increases incrementally, pushing players to play multiple matching cards or draw more cards. The Wild "Double Speed Up" card escalates the intensity by increasing the required card count by two levels and lets the player choose the next color. Action cards like Draw 2, Skip, and Reverse only activate when played as the last card of a player's turn. The speed resets once a player can't keep up, crashing the game's pace and returning it to normal until the next "Speed Up" card is played.
—description from the rulebook (adapted)

item.description:
UNO: Stack Pack Add-On of 16 cards enhances the classic UNO card game by adding stackable draw penalties that increase the game's intensity. Players can use Stack 1 and Stack 2 cards to force the next player to draw one or two cards, respectively, while losing their turn. When responding to other draw cards (+2, +4), these Stack cards can escalate the penalty, making the next player draw even more cards. Wild Stack 3 cards allow players to choose the next color and impose a draw-three penalty on the following player. The unpredictable Wild Stack Number card dramatically heightens the tension by revealing the top number card from the draw pile to determine how many cards the next player must draw. This add-on adds strategic depth and can create significant turnarounds, keeping gameplay exciting.
—description from the rulebook (adapted)

item.description:
UNO: Swap Pack Add-On of 16 cards brings new excitement and unpredictability to the classic UNO card game by introducing unique card-swapping mechanics. Cards such as Swap 1 allow players to exchange a random card with another player's hand. Refresh Hand enables players to completely discard their current hand and draw an equal number of new cards from the draw pile, drastically changing their game strategy. The Wild Force Trade lets a player choose two participants, including themselves, to trade their entire hands, followed by selecting the next play color. Wild Pass Hands dramatically reshapes gameplay by having all players pass their hand to the next player in the current order, again allowing the initiating player to choose the continuing play color. This dynamic add-on makes strategy shifts and sudden game changes frequent, maintaining constant player engagement.
—description from the rulebook (adapted)

item.description:
This is a slight variation on the standard Uno card game, in which you try to be the first to play all the cards in your hand by matching the last discard by color, number, or card type (Wild, Draw 2, Reverse, Skip, etc.).
This version features different dogs for each number card (i.e., all the 1's have one specific dog, all the 2's have another dog, etc.), and each dog is a particular breed as recognized by the American Kennel Club.
This is packaged in one of 4 sets: Terrier Group, Sporting Group, Non-Sporting Group, and Herding Group. Each group showcases dogs from that category of the AKC.
WHAT MAKES IT DIFFERENT FROM TRADITIONAL UNO: The Best in Show card. When you play this card you name a card color (red, yellow, blue, or green). Each player draws a card from the draw deck until he draws a card of the named color. Once all players have done this the player to your left resumes by playing a card of the named color.
